items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic cut their LLM prices by up to 80% within a few months. Why?

score.summary: Speculative essay on why LLM API prices fell sharply across OpenAI and Anthropic models from June to October 2026, with cache-read pricing analysis.
score.whyItMatters: Cache-read price cuts matter for agent cost, but the piece is mostly market speculation about competitor motives rather than config or measured tooling.

items.title: What Adobe v ArtCraft teaches us

score.summary: Discussion of an article on Adobe versus ArtCraft; the item text is only HN comments about Photoshop-style software and AI commoditization.
score.whyItMatters: Covers generative-AI business economics and creative software, outside this reader's interest in agent workflows and Claude Code practice.

items.title: Show HN: ADRs for AI – Deliberation records for human–AI work, versioned in Git

score.summary: Open-source ADR-style template for recording human-AI decisions in Git, with a VS Code extension and an MCP server for agents to query open questions.
score.whyItMatters: The MCP-queryable decision log and ORRCF question format offer a concrete way to keep agent reasoning across multi-repo work, though evidence of results is thin.
score.tryThis: grep -rn '^### QST' docs/adr/ to list open agent-raised questions in a decision record repo.
